g-voice-01.reason: Badges are distributed by someone (no object follows) and 'by the end of next week' requires future, so only the future passive fits.
g-voice-01.why: The missing object and the future time phrase both sit close to the blank; A and B fail on voice, D on tense.

g-voice-02.reason: 'Rise' is intransitive, so with no object the active present perfect 'have risen' is required; 'raise' needs an object and 'rise' has no passive.
g-voice-02.why: Hits the rise/raise learner trap; all four options share 'have', so the choice rests on transitivity rather than tense.

g-voice-03.reason: Ms. Okafor receives the sabbatical from the board (agent 'by the board'), so the passive of ditransitive 'grant' with a retained object is needed.
g-voice-03.why: The noun phrase right after the blank makes the active forms look correct; the deciding 'by' phrase is a few words away.

g-agree-01.reason: 'Every' takes a singular noun and a singular verb, and the clause needs a finite verb.
g-agree-01.why: C and D are non-finite and wrong at a glance, and 'every conference room' is an unmistakable singular with no plural noun between it and the blank.
g-agree-01.fix: Put a plural noun next to the blank to create attraction, e.g. 'Each of the conference rooms on the upper floors ______ a projector and a video camera.' (has / have / having / to have).

g-agree-02.reason: A gerund phrase subject ('Approving refund requests...') is singular and 'usually' calls for simple present, so 'takes'.
g-agree-02.why: The plural nouns 'requests' and 'customers' directly before the blank pull toward 'take'; the true head is the gerund at the start.

g-agree-03.reason: With neither...nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'the two service contracts', which is plural.
g-agree-03.why: Requires knowing the proximity rule; the singular first subject 'the lease agreement' tempts 'requires'.

g-relative-01.reason: A noun ('subscriptions') follows directly and the customers own the subscriptions, so the possessive relative 'whose' is needed.
g-relative-01.why: The noun plus complete clause right after the blank immediately rules out who/whom/which.

g-relative-02.reason: After a quantifier + 'of' in a non-restrictive clause, the object relative for things ('bids') is 'which'.
g-relative-02.why: The antecedent 'bids' is several words back and 'whom' fits the 'two of ___' pattern if the test-taker does not check the antecedent.

g-relative-03.reason: 'Acquired' lacks an object inside the clause, so a relative pronoun ('which') is needed, not the adverb 'where'.
g-relative-03.why: 'Plant' is a place so 'where' fits the words next to the blank; only checking the gap after 'acquired' decides it.

g-pronoun-01.reason: A possessive determiner is needed before the noun phrase 'return policy'.
g-pronoun-01.why: The noun right after the blank settles it; only the its/it's spelling trap adds anything.

g-pronoun-02.reason: The pronoun stands for the plural 'delivery times' and is followed by 'of', so 'those'.
g-pronoun-02.why: 'That of' is a familiar comparison chunk, and the plural antecedent that rules it out is at the start of the sentence.

g-pronoun-03.reason: The blank is the subject standing for 'my reimbursement request' with no noun following, so the possessive pronoun 'mine'.
g-pronoun-03.why: A verb follows immediately, so 'my' has no noun and 'me'/'myself' cannot be subjects.

g-toing-01.why: 'Decided to' is a very high-frequency pattern and the governing verb is right before the blank.

g-toing-02.reason: 'To' in 'in addition to' is a preposition, so it takes a gerund.
g-toing-02.why: Classic preposition-'to' trap: the base form 'edit' looks right after 'to'.

g-toing-03.reason: Causative 'let' + object takes a bare infinitive.
g-toing-03.why: 'To carry out' (by analogy with 'allow') and past 'carried out' (pulled by 'last weekend') are both plausible to learners.

g-compare-01.reason: 'Much ... than' after linking verb 'is' requires a comparative adjective.
g-compare-01.why: 'Than' right after the blank signals the comparative; only the adverb 'more cheaply' offers a mild trap.

g-compare-02.reason: The correlative comparative 'the + comparative ..., the + comparative ...' needs 'the more' in the second half.
g-compare-02.why: Requires recognising the paired structure from the opening 'The earlier'; bare 'more' fits the words next to the blank.

g-compare-03.reason: 'Superior' is a Latinate comparative that takes 'to', not 'than'.
g-compare-03.why: The clue is adjacent but lexical; 'than' is the natural comparative reflex.

g-quantity-01.reason: 'Information' is uncountable, and 'much' is the only option that goes with an uncountable noun, natural in a negative sentence.
g-quantity-01.why: The noun directly after the blank decides it; three options are count-only quantifiers.

g-quantity-02.reason: 'Most of the + plural noun' is correct; 'almost' is an adverb, 'every' cannot take 'of', and 'much' is for uncountables.
g-quantity-02.why: Hits the common almost/most confusion, since 'almost' means roughly the same thing.

g-quantity-03.reason: 'Equipment' is uncountable (confirmed by 'most of it'), so only 'a great deal of' fits.
g-quantity-03.why: Learners often treat 'equipment' as countable, so 'several' and 'a number of' look right.

g-parallel-01.why: 'Both' two words before the blank settles it at a glance.

g-parallel-02.reason: 'Nor' later in the sentence pairs with 'neither'.
g-parallel-02.why: The correlative clue 'nor' is only a few words away and the pairs are well drilled.

g-parallel-03.reason: The list items after 'include' are gerunds ('scheduling', 'updating'), so 'making' keeps them parallel.
g-parallel-03.why: Gerunds on both sides of the blank give the pattern immediately.

g-mandative-01.reason: 'Request that' takes a mandative clause with the base form; the BrE alternatives 'should submit' or 'submits' are not offered.
g-mandative-01.why: 'Will submit' reads naturally with 'by March 15', and base 'submit' after a singular subject looks like an agreement error.

g-mandative-02.reason: 'Essential that' takes the subjunctive, and the negative subjunctive is 'not be'; 'will not be' is not standard in a mandative clause, and 'should not be' or 'is not' are not offered.
g-mandative-02.why: The negative 'not + base' order looks wrong to learners, while 'will not be' sounds natural before 'before it is signed'.
g-mandative-02.fix: Fine to keep as a deliberately hard item. For typical difficulty, use the affirmative: 'It is essential that the draft agreement ______ kept confidential until it is signed.' (be / being / will be / to be).

g-conditional-01.reason: 'Would have found' marks a past counterfactual, and with past participle 'notified' the inverted form is 'Had the supplier notified'.
g-conditional-01.why: All three inversion openers (Should, Had, Were) look plausible; the deciding clues are the verb form 'notified' and the distant 'would have'.

g-conditional-02.reason: A fronted 'Not until...' clause triggers subject-auxiliary inversion, and base form 'begin' after the subject requires 'did'.
g-conditional-02.why: 'Was' echoes 'was installed' just before the blank and 'had' suits the sequence; only the bare 'begin' after the subject decides it.

overall: All 28 items have a single defensible key; I found no item where a British, American or common informal variant makes a second option acceptable (the mandative items avoid offering 'should + verb' or an indicative form, and 'superior than', 'have raised' and neither...nor with a singular verb are not standard). Wording, length and business settings read like real Part 5 throughout, with average style about 4.7. The difficulty mix skews easy-to-medium (11 easy, 13 medium, 4 hard), and all four hard items are in inversion, subjunctive or relative which/where; in my judgment a real Part 5 set has more hard grammar items where the deciding clue is far from the blank. The parallel unit is entirely easy (both-and, neither-nor, gerund list with clues on both sides), and agreement-01 is easier than a real agreement item because nothing intervenes to attract a plural verb. g-conditional-02 tests negative inversion ('Not until ... did'), not a conditional, so it is misfiled under its unit label; g-pronoun-01's 'it's' option is a contraction that real forms seldom use as a distractor.
